data.one_liner: Run FFmpeg and FFprobe commands from Dart on Android, iOS, macOS, Windows and Linux.
data.what_it_does: Provides a Dart API to execute FFmpeg/FFprobe commands across all major desktop and mobile platforms. Includes pre‑built native libraries with full codec support, including GPL codecs, and offers hardware‑accelerated encoding/decoding where available.
use_when: You need to transcode, filter or analyze media files within a Flutter app.
You require GPL‑licensed codecs (e.g., x264, x265) or hardware acceleration on iOS/macOS.
avoid_when: App size must be minimal and you can’t afford the large native binaries.
Your project cannot use GPL‑licensed code due to licensing constraints.
strengths: Full codec set including GPL codecs
Pre‑built native libraries – no manual compilation
Cross‑platform support (Android, iOS, macOS, Windows, Linux)
Hardware‑accelerated video processing on Apple platforms
weaknesses: Large binary size due to bundled libraries
GPL license may be incompatible with some commercial projects
